newsitem.title: UK: London insurers seek to allay electronic fears.
newsitem.headline: London insurers seek to allay electronic fears.

text.p: Backers of LIMNET, an electronic trading support system developed by the London insurance market, have set up a new management structure to underline their support for the project.

"There has been speculation and uncertainty in recent months about the future of LIMNET and its relationship with other networks such as WIN," LIMNET board chairman Dieter Losse said in a statement on Tuesday.
LIMNET's new board includes Lloyd's of London chief executive Ron Sandler and the chairmen of the two leading market associations, Phillip Marcell of LIRMA and Nigel Jenkins of the ILU.

"The creation of the new Board is evidence of the continuing commitment of LIMNET's sponsors to improving the efficiency, effectiveness and accessibility of the London Market through the collective exploitation of electronic commerce."
Other board members include David Hough of the London Insurance Brokers Committee (LIBC), LIMNET deputy chairman Michael Burton and chief executive Kevin Ashby.
LIMNET, which aims to reduce the insurance market paperchase by greater use of technology, has so far met with a slow take-up by market practitioners.
It faces a new challenge next month from the planned launch of World Insurance Network (WIN), an electronic communications system being developed by the world's leading insurance brokers.
Losse said LIMNET was working on a strategic plan, to be considered by the board in October, which will take account of the changing needs and structure of the London market.

In the meantime, LIMNET was committed to its existing electronic placing support (EPS) and electronic counting accounting (ECA) systems, which would not be undermined by new processes and systems, he said.

LIMNET has also entered into a joint venture with WIN and others, including RINET (Reinsurance and Insurance Network), the Brokers and Reinsurers Market Association (BRMA) and the Reinsurance Association of America (RAA), to develop joint standards.
"LIMNET and WIN have agreed areas for further collaboration and a joint statement will be issued later this month," Losse said.
